title: One climate division reversed the annual ozone by moisture injury slope in the Northeast US sample in 1994-2002
abstract: We tested whether whole weather areas determine annual ozone by moisture slope signs in a published forest injury panel. Four eastern US region and period samples used 5,277 site-years in 1994-2010. The same curved model controlled site, year, visit date, temperature, plant count and species count. Removing one climate division changed the early Northeast slope from +0.0492 to -0.0072 injury probability per 10 ppm-h ozone per moisture SD. Every single-site deletion had kept that sign in prior work. Removing two divisions could also reverse the later Northeast and later North Central signs. The early North Central sign survived all one- and two-division removals. These are exact fixed-record sensitivity tests, not confidence intervals or causal effects. Shared weather, selected sites, coarse exposures, missed injury and uncertain full-model slopes limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Whole climate-division deletion ranges in a fixed annual model. Lines are complete finite-sample ranges, not confidence intervals.
